title: Hybrid Circuit Mapping: Leveraging the Full Spectrum of Computational Capabilities of Neutral Atom Quantum Computers
problem: Circuit mapping and routing on neutral atom quantum computers requires optimizing between high-fidelity long-range multi-qubit gates and qubit shuttling. Prior work studies these capabilities separately rather than leveraging both together.
motivation: Combining multiple computational capabilities of neutral atom systems through unified compilation can improve circuit fidelity and compilation efficiency.
method: The paper proposes a fast hybrid compiler that performs circuit mapping and routing by strategically selecting between native multi-qubit gate interactions and qubit shuttling for each operation. The compiler addresses intricacies of combining multiple routing capabilities and optimizes for hardware settings that support both gate-based and shuttle-based routing.
key_novelty: Unified hybrid compilation strategy that integrates gate-based and shuttling-based routing into a single compiler, contrasting with prior approaches that treat these capabilities independently.
contributions: Fast hybrid compiler leveraging both multi-qubit gates and qubit shuttling for circuit mapping
Solutions to handle compilation challenges from combining multiple routing capabilities
Demonstration of fidelity enhancements through strategic combined routing across hardware configurations
Comprehensive methodology for exploiting the full spectrum of neutral atom quantum computer capabilities

metrics.accuracy: fidelity improvements noted but not quantified

limitations: Specific performance limitations and scalability constraints not discussed in abstract
primary_theme: hybrid compilation for neutral atom quantum circuits
